task_1_incidence_forest_definition.vertices: (q, orbit_id) for each E-orbit with orbit_masks[orbit_id] != 0; (h, hexagon_id) for each hexagon targeted by such a registered phase
task_1_incidence_forest_definition.edges: one union per set bit of orbit_masks: bit `phase` of orbit q creates edge (q,q)--(h, hexagon_id(port at that phase))
task_1_incidence_forest_definition.distinguished_hub_root: dec.hub_id (hexagon of the walk's own starting position, fixed per root); has no special status inside incidence_components itself, only in the separate Decoration structure (hub popcount, hub_touch_count, completer)
task_1_incidence_forest_definition.membership_computation: sq, sph = ORBIT_PHASE[pre_state.p] where pre_state is the state after the R2 candidate's own rotation run but before its joint commits; source_present = (q,sq) in the freshly-rebuilt union-find parent dict
task_1_incidence_forest_definition.target_a_usage: Target A (per research/RR_TARGET_A_PRUNE_SCOPE_AUDIT_CODEX.md) is an R2 macro edge whose child has F_def=1, H=0, and whose R2 source and target E-orbits lie in the same incidence-forest component. Source-orbit membership is a precondition for the same-component question to even be well-defined; its absence is reported as its own taxonomy category (r2_wrong_source_orbit), not folded into not_same_component.

task_3_geometry_failure_explanation.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION
task_3_geometry_failure_explanation.interpretation: all 44021 failures descend from exactly one R1 event (fires at macro_index 5, targets orbit 0 i.e. the hub, with its hub completer having fired earlier at macro_index 4 -- the PRE_R_COMPLETER_EVENT_ORDER / provisional-CH0 pattern). Cross-checked against component_failures.json's 5419 records: identical signature (same event_order_class, same r1_target_orbit=0, same ell=5). ALL 49440 R2 candidates in this run, both failure classes, descend from this single event; the other three R1 events contributed zero R2 candidates within this budget.
task_3_geometry_failure_explanation.mechanism: every frontier state's own current orbit is already registered (100% of 85 states, task 5) because a frontier state always stands exactly where its own most recent weight>=2 joint landed, which always sets a bit for its own orbit. It is specifically the ADDITIONAL rotation (0-5 further pure-rotation steps) that an R2 CANDIDATE's own rotation run performs before its joint is tested that can move the position into a different, unregistered E-orbit -- pure rotation never touches orbit_masks (task 2).
task_3_geometry_failure_explanation.open_question_not_resolved: why ell is always exactly 5 in this data, never 0-4, is NOT confirmed from the exported ledgers -- a plausible but unconfirmed hypothesis is that shorter-ell R2-shaped candidates are eliminated by exact_permutation_collision (the dominant prune reason overall, 1541360 occurrences) before ever reaching the R2 recognizer. See export_request below.

could_coarsening_later_repair_the_relati.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION -- explicitly not claiming permanent impossibility
could_coarsening_later_repair_the_relati.statement: not provably either way from this data. Monotonicity (task 2) guarantees a merge, once it happens, is permanent, but does NOT guarantee any specific pair of components ever merges. candidate_edge_would_merge_components=False answers only whether THIS specific already-failing candidate would itself be the merging event -- it says nothing about whether some OTHER later edge (touching a hexagon shared by both components) could still merge them. The exported data is a frontier/failure snapshot, not a full future continuation, so this cannot be checked directly.

task_4_same_component_failures.is_failure_terminal_only_at_that_candida: yes -- chaining (r1.target_orbit == R2.source_orbit) is False for all 5419, and each record is a distinct (pre_state, candidate) pair at a distinct depth; a later R2 attempt from a different position could test a different, larger, or differently-connected source component. Nothing here says a later attempt from this lineage WOULD succeed, only that this data does not rule it out.

task_7_theorem_attempt.label: CLAUDE_OBSERVATION -- theorem is FALSE as stated
task_7_theorem_attempt.candidate_theorem: after the first R event in the short_ell0 root, the only possible second-R source orbits are outside the incidence forest unless a specific transition pattern occurs
task_7_theorem_attempt.verdict: false, and the data itself is the counterexample: 10.96% of observed R2 candidates (5419 of 49440) DO have their source orbit inside the forest -- they fail on not_same_component instead, a different reason entirely
task_7_theorem_attempt.exact_missing_transition_pattern: an R2 candidate whose rotation run lands in an orbit q such that (a) orbit_masks[q] already has at least one set bit from an EARLIER Z2/Z3/R edge in the same walk (ruling out r2_wrong_source_orbit), AND (b) that vertex's component already contains, or is later joined by an intervening edge to, whichever component R1's own target orbit belongs to at that same moment (ruling out not_same_component). This restates Target A's own definition specialized to the two observed failure modes; no exported record satisfies both simultaneously (Target_A_hits=0 confirms this directly).

codex_export_request.label: CLAUDE_PROPOSAL -- an export request, not a search request
codex_export_request.statement: export, for a bounded sample of expanded post-R1 nodes, the rotation-length histogram of every GENERATED edge (not just ones reaching the R2 recognizer), partitioned by which prune reason each ell value received -- specifically whether ell in {0..4} R2-shaped candidates are eliminated by exact_permutation_collision before ever reaching evaluate_edge's R2 branch. This would convert task 3's open hypothesis into either a confirmed mechanism or a genuine counterexample, without any new traversal.
